A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FARM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained experiments and graphics can be matched reliably despite retitling, reformatting, and relocation.

before.justification: V3 reports original FARM results on MoleculeNet, quantum-property prediction, component and fragmentation ablations, and masking experiments, including in its appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds FARM evaluations on seven TDC ADMET tasks.

M1.justification: V4's main text explicitly includes GCN self-loops and averages the contrastive loss over K negatives, while Appendices D.3–D.4 retain v3's formulas. It also newly describes a projection layer. The PDFs do not resolve whether these represent procedural changes or fuller, incompletely reconciled documentation of the existing method.

E1.justification: Section 5.6 and Table 6 add ADMET evaluation on Bioav, AqSol, PPBR, VDss, CYP2C9 inhibition, CYP3A4 inhibition, and Ames. The photostability/quantum-property dataset is the same Angello et al. dataset previously evaluated in v3 Appendix E, rather than additional coverage.

E2.justification: V4 Table 2 adds SCAGE, frozen and finetuned SMI-TED 289M, and HiMol (L); v3's HiMol matches the retained HiMol (S). These substantially expand the benchmark comparisons. Table 6 also introduces ADMET leaderboard comparisons, although individual SOTA methods are not identified there.

E3.justification: The added ADMET evaluation adopts TDC's standardized train/validation/test split and task-specific AUROC, AUPRC, MAE, and Spearman metrics. Existing MoleculeNet scaffold splits and random-split ablation protocols remain unchanged. Newly supplied photostability split details do not establish that the retained experiment was changed.

E4.justification: Component, fragmentation, and masking ablations retain their results, as do vocabulary-growth, attention, embedding, and training-loss analyses. Component results move from v3 Table 10 to v4 Table 4. The ADMET addition is benchmark evaluation, not a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: V3 already reports quantum-property means and standard deviations over ten runs. V4 Section 5.1 newly specifies ten random seeds and repeated scaffold-split construction, without establishing an increase in runs. MoleculeNet's three-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: V4 adds baseline and ADMET results and revises several MolCLR scores, including HIV ROC-AUC from 77.4±0.6 to 88.6±2.2. FARM's retained scores are unchanged, but it is now table-best on six MoleculeNet tasks. ADMET results report first place on AqSol, PPBR, and Ames. Quantum scores differ only in rounding, although new Section 5.3 incorrectly states a minimum R² of 0.815 despite the table's 0.755.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects v3's reversed explanation of ComplEx optimization: positive scores increase and negative scores decrease. V4 also revises the displayed main-text GCN neighborhood and contrastive-loss expressions to include self-loops and K-negative averaging; corresponding appendix expressions are not updated.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list explicitly extend the stated transfer-learning contribution to quantum-property generalization beyond MoleculeNet and materials design, drawing on results already present in v3's appendix. The central FG-aware representation contributions and the claim of state-of-the-art performance on 11 of 13 MoleculeNet tasks remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations connecting BBBP/BACE and solubility performance to functional-group patterns. New ADMET discussion addresses small, imbalanced, mechanistically heterogeneous datasets and motivates selecting particular tasks. It also qualifies its broader-than-textbook use of functional groups. The existing limitation concerning missing full 3D representations is retained.

D1.justification: V4 newly documents annotation pseudocode, deterministic canonicalization, invalid-SMILES filtering, deduplication, and exclusion of MoleculeNet overlap. It supplies photostability holdout details, identifies the three QM9 targets, and explains staged training and projection alignment. These are substantial documentation additions, not evidence of reruns. The code-access link changes from GitHub to an anonymous repository.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to SCAGE, SMI-TED, and MMGX. Related work adds a paragraph positioning SCAGE as supporting functional-group-informed pretraining. The broader positioning against fragmentation approaches and alongside molecular contrastive learning remains intact.

P1.justification: V4 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, expands method explanations, and reorganizes Section 5 into dedicated subsections. Quantum results and component ablations become part of the main narrative. This constitutes extensive editorial and structural revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Separate classification and regression tables become one wide Table 2. Quantum and component tables move into the main text and are reformatted, including a new component-description column. V4 adds ADMET Table 6 and Algorithm 1 and changes typography and float placement. Figures 1–8 retain their graphics.

improvement.justification: Expanded comparisons, ADMET evaluation, and important reproducibility disclosures improve the evidence available to readers. However, the retained 11-of-13 headline, supported by v3's comparisons allowing ties, conflicts with v4 Table 2's six leading results. V4 also introduces the incorrect quantum minimum-R² summary. These useful additions coexist with material reliability problems in the paper's central summaries, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
